chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Rebuke the evil-doer by rewarding the good-doer.

key_terms.الْمُحْسِنِ: The one who does good or excels
key_terms.الْمُسِيءِ: The one who does evil or makes mistakes

ai.seo_question: How can rewarding good people help correct the behavior of wrongdoers?
ai.summary: This maxim, often cited in Shia ethical discourse, employs the principle of *muqabala* (contrast) to induce *hasra* (shame) in the wrongdoer by highlighting their neglect relative to the rewarded. It reflects the strategic wisdom of Imam Ali (AS) in governance, where positive reinforcement serves as a subtle yet powerful corrective mechanism. This approach aligns with the broader Islamic concept of using grace to expose the inadequacy of the ungrateful or erring.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 177. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Rebuke the evil-doer by rewarding the good-doer. [1]
